newsitem.title: USA: CME hog, pork belly futures expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog, pork belly futures expected lower.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open 0.200 to 0.400 cent per lb lower while pork belly futures were called 0.300 to 0.750 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover pressure in hog futures is expected to stem from Friday's limit losses of 2.000 cents per lb in October and December and weak tone in cash markets. Cash hogs are called steady to instances $0.50 per cwt lower and some wholesale pork prices were under pressure Friday, analysts said.
There has also been growing concern over the slower-than-expected Japanese pork buying, they said.
Sources in Japan said pork imports did increase during July, but relatively high U.S. prices kept trade houses from buying U.S. pork amid ideas European pork was quite competitive.
However, the futures market appears somewhat oversold and this may limit any setback, analysts said.

Pork belly futures were also expected to show carryover pressure from Friday's limit setback in February and March. Spot August is also seen showing further losses as it continues to hold a premium to cash. But deliveries remain in strong hands which will provide underlying support to August, they added.
